Form One.competence: 1.1 Demonstrate mastery of the concepts, theories and principles of Business Education
Form One.activity: (a) Describe the concept and scope of business studies, and its relationship with other disciplines

Form One.competence: 1.1 Demonstrate mastery of the concepts, theories and principles of Business Education
Form One.activity: Skills lab: Organise students in manageable groups to identify various clubs that exist in schools. Then, relate their responses to the concept of a school business club, its meaning, importance and how it works. Provide students with the business club guidelines and milestones. Ask each group to work on one component of the simple constitution of a club such as membership, leadership, finance, disputes, and dissolution, and share. Project activity: Task students to compile all the components (developed in the skills lab) into one document. Guide students to make several amendments into a club constitution and use it to formulate the business club. Follow-up on project activity: Let students reflect on what mindsets and skills they had to use to create the constitution and how they might use those skills in the future as entrepreneurs or business owners

Form One.competence: 1.1 Demonstrate mastery of the concepts, theories and principles of Business Education
Form One.activity: (b) Describe the concept and theories of entrepreneurship (meaning, characteristics, skills and importance)

Form One.competence: 1.1 Demonstrate mastery of the concepts, theories and principles of Business Education
Form One.activity: (c) Describe sole proprietorship (meaning, features, advantages and disadvantages and start-up)

Form One.competence: 1.1 Demonstrate mastery of the concepts, theories and principles of Business Education
Form One.activity: Project activity: Task students in a group(s) to write a simple report/presentation on how to register a sole proprietorship in Tanzania. Case study: Provide case studies on sole proprietor business start-up processes of a real person (from capital acquisition, the business idea, resources needed, customers and market). Guide students in pairs to discuss and share some things they would consider when starting up their own businesses

Form Three.competence: 1.1 Demonstrate mastery of the concepts, theories and principles of Business Education
Form Three.activity: Group activity: Organise students in manageable groups to identify any business activity in their community or their business club, and show how the business owner influence customers about their products or services and increases Let groups share their responses with the rest of class. Then, relate their responses to the meaning of marketing and its importance. Case study: Provide a case study that portrays the marketing activities of an operating small business in the community. The case study should indicate the 4Ps (product, price, place/ distribution and promotion). Let students analyse the given case study and then answer questions related to the identified 4Ps of marketing

Form Three.competence: 1.1 Demonstrate mastery of the concepts, theories and principles of Business Education
Form Three.activity: Skills lab: Organise students in manageable groups to prepare a marketing plan using the 4Ps for business club products. Let students present their marketing plans to the rest of the class. Project activity: Task students to use the 4Ps to market their products made in their business club. From time to time, monitor the progress

Form Three.competence: 1.1 Demonstrate mastery of the concepts, theories and principles of Business Education
Form Three.activity: Scenario: Prepare a scenario that portrays the meaning and importance of e-marketing. Guide students to summarise the lessons learned from the scenario and relate their discussion with the meaning and importance of e-marketing. Group activity: Organise students in manageable groups to discuss features of e-marketing which enable small businesses to operate effectively. Let students make presentations for common understanding. Relate their presentations with the features of e-marketing

Form Three.competence: 1.1 Demonstrate mastery of the concepts, theories and principles of Business Education
Form Three.activity: Group activity: Organise students in manageable groups to discuss the meaning of biography and social media. Let students share their findings from the discussions. Relate their presentations with the meaning of biography and social media. Guide students on how to create social media accounts. Skills lab: Using a template containing the features of a good biography, then ask students in manageable groups to discuss and design their business biography to uploaded in social media. Let students present their biographies and provide the feedback for improvements. Guide students to upload the biographies on their business club social media accounts

Form Three.competence: 1.1 Demonstrate mastery of the concepts, theories and principles of Business Education
Form Three.activity: Project activity: Task students to create individual social media accounts and upload their individual business biography. Guest speaker: Invite a resourceful person to share on how they use e-marketing to market their business. Let students write a report on the lessons learnt from the presentation

Form Three.main: 2.0 Solve social challenges using business skills
Form Three.competence: 2.1 Demonstrate mastery of the basic skills of operating a small-scale business
Form Three.activity: Group activity: Discuss school rules and regulations controlling club activities. Relate the findings from the discussions to the meaning and importance of regulations governing small business operations in Tanzania. Case study: Provide a case study portraying a business which does not pay tax & levies and sells illegal products. Guide students to analyse the case study and discuss the possible consequences for non-compliances and certification. Then discuss basic certifications and compliances procedures to consider when starting and running a business in Tanzania. Let students share their findings from group discussions. Summarise the students’ presentations by relating to the importance of compliance and certification and the basic certification and compliance procedures required to consider when starting or running a business in Tanzania. Guide students to discuss additional regulatory policies and government institutions and agencies that guide business operations in Tanzania. Guest speaker: Invite a resourceful person from government agencies responsible for regulating small business operations in Tanzania and share the following: (i) Government agencies relating with businesses in Tanzania (ii) roles of such agencies (iii) Business regulations (laws, policies) (iv) importance of complying with the regulations. Project activity: Task students in manageable groups to reflect on the guest speaker presentations by writing and submitting a report with recommendations on how they can comply with business regulations in their business club

Form Three.main: 2.0 Solve social challenges using business skills
Form Three.competence: 2.1 Demonstrate mastery of the basic skills of operating a small-scale business
Form Three.activity: Reflection: Guide students to recall the importance of business compliance and certification. Relate their responses to types of licenses, importance of registration and certification and compliance. Field trip: Guide students to visit nearest businesses and find out types of licenses they have, importance of registration and consequences of non-compliance. Let them ask where they register their businesses (sole proprietorship) and thereafter discuss how the businesses are legally registered. Resourceful person: Invite a staff working at district/agency who is in charge of supervising businesses registration and licensing in the community. The resource person should share on: (i) Procedure for registration and licensing a business (ii) Penalties for non-compliance. Skills lab: Get the students into manageable groups and provide students with a business registration guide and assign them to create an action plan on the steps they will take to register their businesses with relevant authorities. Project activity: Task students in manageable groups to prepare the procedures of registering a business of their choice, then discuss or foresee the registration challenges they may encounter and the mitigation plan

Form Three.main: 3.0 Apply business knowledge in various contexts
Form Three.activity: Brainstorm: Organise students in manageable groups to brainstorm on the meaning and importance of planning. Relate students’ responses to the meaning and importance of business planning. Case study: Organise students in manageable groups and provide a case study that portrays the plan for a small business from the community or business club. The case study should capture areas of business description, operating activities, market analysis and marketing plan. Let students discuss and share lessons learnt from the case study. Skills lab: Organise students in manageable groups to develop a plan that shows business description, market analysis, operating activities and marketing plan. Let students present their plans to receive feedback for further improvements. Group activity: Provide students with templates of management, organisation, operations and financial plans. Let students discuss and reflect what they learned in the previous classes to create their own plans and share with the rest of class through presentation. Skills lab: Organise students in manageable groups to develop management, organisation, operations and financial plans for their identified small businesses using relevant templates shared to them. Let students present their plans to receive feedback for further improvements. Project activity: Task students in manageable groups or individually to create a business plan for their small business that includes business description, market analysis, marketing, management, organisation, operations and financial plans

Form Three.main: 3.0 Apply business knowledge in various contexts
Form Three.competence: 3.2 Demonstrate mastery of basic business ethics
Form Three.activity: Brainstorming: Organise students in manageable groups to brainstorm on the norms and values that exist in their community. Relate their responses to the meaning and importance of ethics (norms and values) in operating businesses in Tanzania. Skills lab: Organise students in manageable groups to discuss and write personal values that influence business operations. Then, let them discuss and present how they will promote those values in the business club activities. Let students develop ethics guides for their businesses. Project activity: Task students in manageable groups to write a report on the impact of bad/poor personal values on the business operations and draw/develop a plan of how they can help the business owner to improve. Group activity: Guide students in manageable groups to search the business ethics advocated by Fair competition commission (FCC) and Zanzibar Fair competition commission (ZFCC), let them discuss in a class. Then, summarise and conclude the basic tenets of ethics applicable for small businesses in Tanzania

Form Four.competence: 1.1 Demonstrate mastery of the concepts, theories and principles of Business Education
Form Four.activity: (a) Explain the basic aspects of insurance for small businesses (meaning, principles, importance, choice of appropriate insurance plan and procedures of filing insurance claims) Scenario: Share a short story to the students concerning different damages in a community. Then, guide students to relate the findings in the scenario by identifying: (i) Risks identified in the story; and (ii) Means of overcoming risks Relate their feedback to the meaning and importance of insurance Guest speaker: Invite a resource person, who is an expert on insurance, to come and share with students on the following: (i) principles of insurance; (ii) types of insurance; (iii) choice of appropriate insurance plan; (iv) procedures of obtaining insurance policy; and (v) procedures for filing insurance claims Let students write a report on what they learnt from the resource person in relation to principles of insurance, types of insurance and procedures for filing insurance claims Skills lab: Use manageable groups to discuss how they can obtain insurance for their business club and what strategies they can use to achieve this goal Project activity: Task students to show how they will apply their knowledge of insurance to obtain an insurance for their businesses and properties

Form Four.competence: 1.1 Demonstrate mastery of the concepts, theories and principles of Business Education
Form Four.activity: (b) Describe business partnerships (meaning, types, features, advantages and disadvantages, formation and dissolution) Role play: Use manageable groups to role play features associated with running a business as a group Relate the role play to the meaning, features and formation of business partnership Case study: Provide a case study that portrays a partnership business. The case study should capture areas of formation and dissolution of a partnership. Let students discuss and share lessons learnt from the case study Debate: Guide the students to debate on this theme: “Running a business as a group is better than running it as an individual” Relate the students’ arguments in the debate to the advantages and disadvantages of partnership Skills lab: Guide students, in manageable groups, to develop a partnership deed using a partnership deed template provided to them. Let students present their draft partnership deed to receive feedback for further improvement Project activity: Guide the students to polish the partnership deed and use it in their business club. Monitor the progress from time to time

Form Four.main: 2.0 Solve social challenges using business skills
Form Four.competence: 2.1 Demonstrate mastery of the basic skills of operating a small-scale business
Form Four.activity: (a) Describe taxes and levies associated with small businesses in Tanzania (meaning, types, importance, and sanctions for non-compliance) Role play: Direct students to act out a short play depicting a busy market in which tax/levy payers and collectors are in action. Then, ask the students to reflect on the meaning and importance of tax, and sanctions for non-compliance Guest speaker: Invite tax/levies officers from Local government and/or Tanzania Revenue Authority (TRA)/Zanzibar Revenue Authority (ZRA) to share their knowledge and experience on tax and levy issues Prepare guiding questions for the students based on the following: (i) Types of tax; and (ii) Tax assessment Summarise the lesson by linking the guest speaker’s experience to the types of tax and tax assessment Skills lab: Assign students to reflect on specific types of taxes/levies and tell how they can adopt (some of) them in their business club Let student present to the rest of class for feedback Project activity: Task students to write a report on the taxes and levies associated with small businesses in Tanzania

Form Four.main: 2.0 Solve social challenges using business skills
Form Four.competence: 2.1 Demonstrate mastery of the basic skills of operating a small-scale business
Form Four.activity: (b) Describe the basic principles of communication and networking for small businesses Brainstorm activity: Guide students to think about two friends, how they became friends, and how they communicate Relate their responses to the meaning, importance, and channels of communication Scenario: Provide two short write ups such as a business letter or business plan (ideally one page), one with clear communication depicting all communication principles and another with unclear, confusing communication with grammatical errors Guide them to compare the two and identify which one is clearer and why. Relate the findings in the scenario to principles of communication Brainstorm Activity on networking: Guide students to share how they make new friends, why they make friends, and how helpful those friendships have been Relate their responses to the meaning and importance of business networking Skills lab: Task the students to create and write a plan on a loose sheet about how they will use principles of communication and business networking to grow their business project, which they will execute in their business clubs. Through the gallery walk, guide students to present the plans and receive feedback

Form Four.main: 2.0 Solve social challenges using business skills
Form Four.competence: 2.2 Demonstrate mastery of the basic skills of trading locally and internationally
Form Four.activity: (a) Use pricing techniques to determine appropriate prices of products Scenario: Organise students in manageable groups and give each of them a scenario that portrays one type of pricing technique: (i) Cost-plus pricing; (ii) Value pricing; (iii) Penetration pricing; (iv) Price skimming; (v) Bundle pricing; (vi) Premium pricing; (vii) Competitive pricing; and (viii) Psychological pricing Guide students to summarise the lessons learnt from the scenario and relate the discussion with the meaning and importance of various pricing techniques. Field visit: Guide students to visit the nearest producer to investigate how demand, supply, cost, and competition influences the price determination of products Ask students to write a report based on a template provided by the teacher on what they have observed at the market and recommend on how they will price their business products based on the pricing techniques. Skills lab: Guide students, in manageable groups, to choose one product from their project and price it based on the techniques obtained from the scenario and/or field trip Let students present in order to receive feedback Project activity: Task students to create a price catalogue for their products based on the pricing techniques learnt

Form Four.main: 2.0 Solve social challenges using business skills
Form Four.competence: 2.2 Demonstrate mastery of the basic skills of trading locally and internationally
Form Four.activity: (b) Identify relevant procedures and practices for buying and selling products within and outside the country Scenario: Provide a short scenario of two young people whereby one wishes to sell a product to a neighbouring country and the other wishes to buy another product from that country but they are stranded because they do not have the know-how. Ask the students to advise the two young people Relate the advice from the students to the import and export procedures Case study: Organise students in manageable groups and provide two case studies that portray relevant exporting and importing procedures and practices. The cases should capture the areas of documentation, institutions, clearing and forwarding agencies, and incoterms. Let students discuss and share lessons learnt from the case study

Form Four.main: 2.0 Solve social challenges using business skills
Form Four.competence: 2.2 Demonstrate mastery of the basic skills of trading locally and internationally
Form Four.activity: (c) Use appropriate selling methods and techniques (branding, logos, packaging, after sales services, barcoding, direct mail and internet auctions) to facilitate trade Brainstorm: Guide students to share their experiences of buying and selling products or what they see happening in the community Relate the brainstorm results to the selling methods and techniques in preparation for the skills lab Skills lab: In groups let students choose one product from their club and then name the product, create/finetune the logo, design/improve packaging for the product and barcoding. Also, guide students to propose strategies of selling their products Then, guide students to present in class and provide feedback for further improvement of their proposal Project activity: Guide students in their manageable groups to go and improve products in their business club based on the lesson learnt from the skills lab

Form Four.main: 3.0 Apply business knowledge in various contexts
Form Four.activity: Complete and present the business plan developed in Form Three Group activity: Guide students to exchange their group business plan documents for peer review and further improvement. Students improve their business plans based on the peer feedback Provide feedback and allow them to complete their business plans in their skills lab Skills lab: Guide the students to polish and submit complete business plans. Task students in groups to prepare the pitch of their business plans, role play (rehearse) it, and pitch their business plans in the business club or to a panel of investors Project activity: Let the students prepare and present their portfolio folder comprising all useful documents covered in form four and submit them for assessment
